content: Letter 28, to the ruler of Mazandaran at Sari, i.e., Sayyid Murtażā Marʿashī (ca. 831-32/1428-29, Mazandaran): a pained account of the tribulations of the author and his family in exile that asks the ruler's support in the form of a stipend (dāranda), since scholars' work depends wholly on royal patronage. He says he passed through Gilan, found it uncongenial and went straight to Sari; that he, an innocent scholar, was punished (imprisoned?) for a full year despite the intercession of various amirs and notables. A break with an interjected huwa suggests two letters combined: one asking an audience, one written after it was granted, thanking the ruler for a gracious welcome that eased the pain of exile, describing two days in attendance with every respect shown, and agreeing to stay two more at the ruler's insistence (TMN/MS pp. 21-23, TMN/D pp. 190-94). MK's footnote: Murtażā Marʿashī (d. 837/1433) ruled at Sari 820-37/1417-33.
